title: What counts as an acceptable offer to counsel for third party payment programs
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, § 21A provides that for the purposes of medical assistance and other third party reimbursements or payment programs, any of the above methods, or a combination thereof, shall constitute an acceptable offer to provide counseling. The sentence stands immediately after the paragraphs stating the face to face and telephone offer methods with their needs-or-availability alternative, and the toll-free telephone service pathway for a person who elects delivery at a location other than a pharmacy.
exam_relevance: Names the one place the counseling statute speaks to payment programs, and states that it validates the offer methods already given rather than adding a further method or a further condition.
common_confusions: The sentence says a method already stated in the section is an acceptable offer for payment purposes; it does not create a separate billing-specific offer duty.
A combination of the stated methods is expressly acceptable, so using more than one is not a defect.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21A on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
